title: NEB Class 12 English — Language Development — 2024
subject: english
source: NEB Grade 12 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Forests are often called the lungs of the earth, yet their value is rarely measured in the language of markets. A standing forest prevents landslides, recharges springs, shelters pollinators and stores carbon; a cleared slope yields timber once and then costs the community every monsoon. Nepal's community forestry programme was built on this insight: when the people who live beside a forest manage it, they protect what a distant contractor would remove.

(a) Why is the market value of a forest misleading? (b) State two services a standing forest provides. (c) What was the insight behind community forestry? (d) Find a word in the passage that means 'a person who supplies goods under contract'.
questions.solution:
(a) Because markets price only the timber that can be sold, while the forest's real benefits — preventing landslides, recharging springs, sheltering pollinators and storing carbon — are never bought or sold.

(b) Any two: it prevents landslides; it recharges springs; it shelters pollinators; it stores carbon.

(c) That the people who live beside a forest will protect it, whereas a distant contractor removes it for one-time profit.

(d) 'contractor'.
questions.knowledgeNote: Comprehension answers must be in your own words and supported by the text; copying whole sentences without answering the point loses marks.

questions.question: Write, in about 120 words, a summary of the passage in the first question.
questions.solution: The passage argues that forests are undervalued because markets count only the timber they yield. Their real worth lies in preventing landslides, recharging springs, supporting pollinators and storing carbon — benefits a cleared slope destroys forever. Nepal's community forestry shows the remedy: when local people manage the forest beside them, they protect it, whereas an outside contractor takes what can be sold and leaves. The lesson is that sustainable management depends on the people who bear the consequences, not on distant profit.
questions.knowledgeNote: A summary keeps the central argument and order, drops examples and repetition, and stays within the word limit — do not add opinions.

questions.question: Choose the correct option to complete the sentences: (a) Neither the teacher nor the students ___ (was/were) informed. (b) The meeting was postponed ___ (because of/due to) heavy rain. (c) She is used to ___ (work/working) late.
questions.solution:
(a) **were** — with 'neither … nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject 'students' (plural).

(b) **because of** — 'because of' is a two-word preposition followed by a noun phrase; 'due to' typically follows the verb 'be' (the postponement was due to rain).

(c) **working** — 'be used to' is followed by a gerund (accustomed to it), unlike 'used to work' (past habit).
questions.knowledgeNote: The distinction between 'used to + infinitive' (past habit) and 'be used to + gerund' (accustomed) is a favourite grammar item.
